title: Statement Terms for Northgate Card Accounts: Payment Due Date and Minimum Payment Figures
content:
Every monthly statement on a **Northgate Card Credit Accounts (issued by Harbor Point Bank, N.A.)** account shows a payment due date and a minimum payment due. The three statement figures each card carries are set out below.

| Card | Calendar days from the statement closing date to the payment due date (at least 21 by law) | Floor of the minimum payment due (the whole new balance when the balance is lower) | Percent of the new balance (excluding disputed amounts) that, plus that cycle's interest and fees, forms the minimum payment when it exceeds the floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| Northgate Secured Card | 25 | 30.00 USD | 1% |
| Northgate Store Card | 25 | 40.00 USD | 1% |
| Northgate Mastercard | 25 | 40.00 USD | 1% |
| Northgate World Mastercard | 25 | 40.00 USD | 1% |
| Northgate Business Store Card | 25 | 40.00 USD | 2% |
| Northgate Business Mastercard | 25 | 40.00 USD | 2% |

**Reading the table.**

- The payment due date falls 25 calendar days after the closing date on every card. Hypothetical illustration: a statement closing on the 3rd of a 30-day month is due on the 28th of that month.
- The floor is the smallest minimum payment a card asks for. It is 30.00 USD on the Northgate Secured Card and 40.00 USD on every other card; where the new balance itself is lower than the floor, the whole new balance is the floor.
- The percentage is 1% on the four consumer cards and 2% on the two business cards. It is applied to the new balance with disputed amounts left out, and that cycle's interest and fees are added to the result before it is compared with the floor.

Hypothetical comparison on a new balance of 2000.00 USD with nothing in dispute and 25.00 USD of interest and fees in the cycle: 1% of the balance is 20.00, plus 25.00 gives 45.00, above the 40.00 floor on a consumer Mastercard; on a business card 2% gives 40.00, plus 25.00 gives 65.00.
